I'm testing out the new functionality, but still not entirely sure how to configure it for my scenario in the OP. This is the flow I'm seeing now:

1. Open OpenCode TUI.
2. Connect provider.
3. Select Azure.
4. Select Entra ID.
5. It uses the Azure CLI to look for my credentials, that works.
6. It presents me a list of resource names. I select the Foundry.
7. I get the model selection, I select a model that I know should work.
8. I ask a test question and get `PermissionDenied` without further details.

The customer I'm working for has a bit of a special setup:
1. They have a custom Azure API Management service hosted at `https://their-custom-domain.azure-api.net/` that seems to forward all calls (so `/ai/*`) to `https://their-actual-foundry-swedencentral-001.cognitiveservices.azure.com` (so e.g. Claude CLI uses `https://their-custom-domain.azure-api.net/ai/anthropic`).
2. On this API forwarding rule, they have a rule `validate-azure-ad-token` set.

In other words they don't seem to support directly using the Foundry URL in question and Entra-authenticated calls need to go through a custom URL/domain instead. Is there any way to configure `opencode.jsonc` to use the new Entra authentication instead of an API key? The main problem seems to be that I need to be able to enter a fully custom URL (as opposed to just a resource name).

I traced the current dev request path and tested a local bounded-request prototype. A timeout alone is not sufficient: converting timeout or initialization failures to [] or null preserves the central problem reported here, because failure still looks like a successful empty result.

A complete fix should distinguish a healthy empty response from server-unavailable, initialization-failed, and request-timeout states. I can contribute a fake nonresponsive LSP regression test once the desired error shape is decided.

I also found a separate workspace-symbol routing problem: the tool accepts filePath but workspaceSymbol ignores it and queries only already-active clients. I am filing that separately so it does not broaden this issue.

This still reproduces on `v0.0.0-beta-18721` (this was closed after testing `beta-18050`), and on a different platform — macOS 26.6.2 arm64, vs the original Linux x86_64 report. Filed as #46358 with full detail.

Adding one test that wasn't in the original report and that should address the "prompting/tool-selection problem" possibility raised when this was closed:

**In a single Plan-mode session, with two paths that both have matching `allow` rules in the agent's resolved permissions:**

| Target | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.opencode/plan/003-example.md` | `Cannot use write to modify files outside the Plan directory: /Users/<user>/.opencode/plan` |
| `~/aidocs/guard-probe.md` | succeeded |

The same tool, in the same session, writes successfully to one path and is refused for the other. So the tool call is being issued correctly — this is not tool selection or prompting — and it is not a blanket Plan-mode write block. The guard discriminates by path and does not recognise `~/.opencode/plan` as the plan directory it names in its own error message.

The path that succeeds is project-relative; the one that fails is absolute. That is consistent with the unnormalized/wrongly-based comparison hypothesis in the original report.

One environmental detail that may explain why this didn't reproduce on your side: **the session's working directory here is the user's home directory (`/Users/<user>`), which is also the detected project root**, and the plan directory `~/.opencode/plan` therefore sits underneath it. If the guard derives the plan directory from the project/session location rather than the advertised absolute path, a home-directory session seems a plausible trigger. Might be worth testing with the session rooted at `$HOME`.

Also relevant: `~/.opencode` here contains `memory/`, `node_modules/`, `package.json`, and `.gitignore` alongside `plan/`, and the plan directory has pre-existing files in it.

I don't have a shareable session transcript, which is what was requested — but the contrast above should serve the same diagnostic purpose.

I’m experiencing what appears to be the same underlying issue, but on Windows and with a directory rename rather than moving the project to a different location.

Reproduction:

1. Add `D:\Projects\my-project` as a workspace in OpenCode.
2. Rename the directory externally using Windows File Explorer:
   `my-project` → `my-project-renamed`
3. The existing workspace becomes unusable.
4. Remove the old workspace from OpenCode.
5. Add `D:\Projects\my-project-renamed` as a new workspace.
6. The newly added workspace is still unusable.
7. Rename the directory back to `my-project`.
8. The workspace immediately works again.

So even after removing the old workspace and adding the new path, OpenCode appears to retain or resolve some state against the original path/name.

This seems closely related to this issue, although in my case the path only changes because the directory is renamed, not moved to another location.

Environment:

* Windows
* OpenCode GUI

Confirming with a billing-level reconciliation (opencode 1.18.25, Linux; deepseek-v4-pro behind a custom provider config).

I ran a session that fanned out 3 subagents via the Task tool, then walked `parent_id` in the SQLite history and cross-checked the whole tree against the provider's billing export for that day:

| | API calls | cost (opencode rates) |
|---|---|---|
| Root session — the only part the sidebar shows | 143 | $0.168 |
| Subagent 1 | 21 | $0.0417 |
| Subagent 2 | 16 | $0.0395 |
| Subagent 3 | 23 | $0.0396 |
| **True total** | **203** | **$0.2887** |

Subagents were 42% of the session's real cost — none of it visible in the sidebar, `opencode stats`, or `/export`. Same as reported.

The provider export also lets us verify the tree itself is complete: billed cache-hit tokens for the day are 19,509,632 — matching root + all 3 subagents to the exact token. Two side observations from the same reconciliation:

- Exactly one billed request appears in no session at all: the session-title generation call (752 in / 498 out). That's #7175.
- The gap between opencode's estimate and the actual bill is large for this model ($0.2887 estimated vs $1.688 billed). That's the pricing side (#7387). The two issues compound: combined, the sidebar showed ~10× less than what the provider actually charged.

Happy to share the exact SQL/queries used for the reconciliation if that helps.

Reviewed against a billing-reconciled session tree (root + 3 subagents, cross-checked against the provider's invoice — context in #45417): the BFS rollup with the visited set is correct, fork zeroing works, and the test coverage (nested / multi-child / fork scenarios) is good. One real issue in the stats aggregation:

**`opencode stats` grand total double-counts child sessions.**

`getAllSessions()` returns every row from the session table (no `parentID` filter), and the aggregate does `stats.totalCost += result.sessionCost` per session. With this PR a top-level session contributes `totalCost` (own + all descendants) while its children still contribute their own `session.cost` — every child is counted twice in the grand total.

Numbers from my reconciled tree (root $0.168 own + children $0.0417 / $0.0395 / $0.0396):

- correct total: **$0.2887**
- `stats.totalCost` with this PR: 0.2887 + 0.1208 = **$0.4095** (+42%)

Suggested fix: contribute 0 from child rows to the grand total when their parent is present in the aggregated set (or only aggregate top-level rows). Per-session rows can still display each session's own cost.

Two smaller notes:

- Fork zeroing sets cloned `step-finish` parts to cost 0, so inside a fork the inherited messages display as free. Reasonable for "what has this fork spent since forking", but worth a line in the description since per-message cost display changes meaning after a fork.
- Hidden LLM calls (title/summary generation) remain outside both `session.cost` and `totalCost` — tracked in #46371; not a defect of this PR, but relevant to anyone reconciling stats against invoices.

Thanks for picking this up. This shares the same root cause as #41972 ("Sessions silently deleted after cross-session API access", closed as not planned) — that issue surfaced the true trigger verbatim:

> `ERROR "Failed to drain Session" sessionID=... cause="ModelUnavailableError: Model unavailable: opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash"`

Here is the **raw app log** (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`) for the exact incident window in my case (only the username is redacted). It shows the stream failure, the teardown, and the restart during which the session's messages were purged:

```
11417 20:54:57  INFO  message=stream providerID=opencode modelID=deepseek-v4-flash-free session.id=ses_013f03c75ffe47d0pOqHvTNmcb
11419 20:54:58  ERROR message="stream error" providerID=opencode modelID=deepseek-v4-flash-free
                error.error="AI_APICallError: Error from provider (Console): Upstream request failed: Model is unavailable."
11420 20:54:58  ERROR message=process ... error="... Model is unavailable." stack="AI_APICallError: ...\n at ...app.asar/out/main/chunks/node-coyY5_xs.js"
11421 20:55:03  INFO  message="global event disconnected"
11422 20:55:03  INFO  message="disposing all instances"
11423 20:55:03  INFO  message="disposing instance" directory=/Users/<redacted>
11425 20:55:03  INFO  message="disposing instance" directory=/
11426 20:55:10  INFO  message=loading ... (app restarts) run changed 54f46cec -> 984c9373 -> 3623fab5
...
11474 20:56:42  INFO  message=loop session.id=ses_013f03c75ffe47d0pOqHvTNmcb step=0   (<-- new thread, history gone)
```

Between the teardown (`disposing all instances`) at 20:55:03 and the new loop at 20:56:42, the session's `message`/`part` rows were physically deleted — a burst of `message.removed.1` events in the DB's event log (seq 118–130, then 140–141).

The one thing worth keeping separate from the #41972 thread: **#41972 reproduces via the SDK / cross-session API path, while mine happened in the plain Desktop GUI during ordinary single-session use** — no cross-session access at all. So this isn't limited to the bridge/SDK path; a normal GUI user can hit it too whenever a streaming model errors.

DB-level detail for anyone triaging (session `ses_013f03c75ffe47d0pOqHvTNmcb`):

- affected rows were **genuinely deleted, not just hidden from the UI** — this distinguishes it from the #34471 family where the DB stays intact
- the full text survives only in the `event` table (last `message.updated.1` / `message.part.updated.1` per id), which is how I reconstructed the history
